issues.failure_explanation: The same index $j$ is used both as the vertical level in the coefficient $\bar a_i(y_j)$ and as the horizontal interpolation-node index in $\psi_i(x_j)=\delta_{i,j}$. Moreover, one globally defined function $\psi_i(x)$ solving a constant-coefficient second-order ODE cannot in general satisfy cardinal conditions at every horizontal node, while the displayed finite-difference operator requires coefficients that vary by horizontal interval and vertical row. Thus $T^N$, and hence the Petrov-Galerkin problem, is not defined as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define row-dependent, piecewise exponential functions with distinct horizontal and vertical indices and the appropriate intervalwise values of $\bar a$, or explicitly take the finite-difference system as the definition of the method and establish its equivalence to a corrected Petrov-Galerkin formulation.
issues.overall_effect: The stated finite-element method and the theorem's reference to its solution are formally ill-defined, although the separately displayed finite-difference scheme indicates the likely intended executable method.
issues.title: The exponential test space is not well defined
issues.why_classification: The finite-difference stencil already supplies the intended discrete method, so a local correction of the test-space definition can preserve the algorithm and all advertised rates without new analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: The positive coefficient in the preceding bound is $\frac{\ve}{h_i}\sigma(\bar\rho_i)=\alpha/(1-e^{-\bar\rho_i})$. Since $h_i\ge h_{i+1}$ gives $\bar\rho_i\ge\bar\rho_{i+1}$, this coefficient is at most, not at least, $\alpha/(1-e^{-\bar\rho_{i+1}})$. At the coarse-to-fine transition, take a nondecreasing mesh function with $D_x^-Z(x_i)>0$ and $D_x^+Z(x_i)=0$; the asserted right-hand side can be much larger than the available positive term. Thus the stated inequality does not follow and is generally false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Corollary 1 by a valid nonuniform-mesh estimate retaining the distinct $h_i$ and $h_{i+1}$ coefficients, and reverify the exponential barrier functions—especially at the coarse-to-fine transition—before reusing the discrete minimum principle.
issues.overall_effect: The barrier inequalities for the regular, characteristic, and corner layer errors are not established at the horizontal transition point, so their nodal estimates and the resulting global convergence theorem are unsupported.
issues.title: Corollary 1 reverses the mesh-step comparison in its lower bound
issues.why_classification: A comparable result may survive through direct transition-point estimates, but the repair requires a contained nontrivial barrier analysis rather than a purely algebraic edit.

issues.failure_explanation: Summing the displayed component equations gives $L^N(V+\sum W)=f(x_i,y_j)$, whereas the actual discrete solution satisfies the quadrature-weighted right-hand side $\bar h_i^{-1}(Q^-_{i,j}\bar f_{i,j}+Q^+_{i,j}\bar f_{i+1,j})$. These are not equal for general nonconstant $f$. Consequently the asserted identity $U=V+W_E+W_N+W_S+W_{EN}+W_{ES}$ is false as defined, so componentwise estimates cannot be summed to bound the numerical solution $U$.
